blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Tendulkar shifted poverty estimation to uniform mixed reference period consumption, while Rangarajan restored nutrition norms and NITI Aayog adopted multidimensional MPI.

blocks.content: 🗺️ Modern Poverty Line Reform: Tendulkar vs. Rangarajan vs. National MPI

1. Suresh Tendulkar Committee (2009): Shifted away from calorie anchor. Used **Urban Basket** as uniform baseline. Adopted **Mixed Recall Period (MRP)**. Poverty line: **₹27/day (Rural)** & **₹33/day (Urban)** [₹816 & ₹1000/month]. 2011-12 Poverty = **21.9%**.

2. C. Rangarajan Committee (2014): Restored nutrition norms (calories + protein + fat) + non-food requirements. Adopted **Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP)**. Poverty line: **₹32/day (Rural)** & **₹47/day (Urban)** [₹972 & ₹1407/month]. 2011-12 Poverty = **29.5%**.
3. NITI Aayog National MPI (2021/2023): Non-monetary multidimensional measure using NFHS data across **12 indicators**.

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Tendulkar vs. Rangarajan Committees Benchmark Comparison
| Parameter | Suresh Tendulkar Committee (2009) | C. Rangarajan Committee (2014) |
|---|---|---|
| **Calorie Anchor** | **Abandoned explicit calorie anchor** | **Restored calorie + protein + fat norms** (Rural: 2155 kcal, Urban: 2090 kcal) |
| **Recall Period Used** | Mixed Recall Period (MRP - 365-day for low-frequency items) | Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP - 7-day for edible oil/veg, 30-day for rest) |
| **Rural Poverty Line (2011-12)** | **₹27 / day** (₹816 per capita per month) | **₹32 / day** (₹972 per capita per month) |
| **Urban Poverty Line (2011-12)** | **₹33 / day** (₹1,000 per capita per month) | **₹47 / day** (₹1,407 per capita per month) |
| **Poverty Headcount (2011-12)** | **21.9%** (269.8 million poor) | **29.5%** (363 million poor) |
| **Price Index Used** | Fisher Ideal Index | Independent State-level CPI-AL and CPI-IW |

📖 2. NSSO Recall Periods Explained
- **Uniform Recall Period (URP):** Asks respondents about consumption expenditure over a uniform **30-day recall period** for all goods. *(Used pre-2005)*.
- **Mixed Recall Period (MRP):** Uses 30-day recall for general goods, but **365-day recall** for 5 non-food low-frequency items (clothing, footwear, durable goods, education, institutional medical). *(Used by Tendulkar)*.
- **Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP):** Uses **7-day recall** for highly volatile food items (edible oil, eggs, meat, vegetables, fruits), 365-day for 5 non-food items, and 30-day for remaining items. *(Used by Rangarajan & current NSO MPCE surveys)*.

🏛️ 3. NITI Aayog National MPI Architecture & Progress
- **Data Source:** NFHS-4 (2015-16) & NFHS-5 (2019-21) health surveys.
- **12 Indicators:** Nutrition, Child & Adolescent Mortality, Maternal Health, Years of Schooling, School Attendance, Cooking Fuel, Sanitation, Drinking Water, Electricity, Housing, Assets, Bank Accounts.
- **Reported Trend (NITI Aayog 2023 Update):** 13.5 Crore Indians exited multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21 (MPI headcount ratio dropped from 24.85% to 14.96%).

⚖️ 4. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** Official government poverty estimates in India for 2011-12 are still based on the **Tendulkar Committee line (21.9%)**, because Rangarajan Committee recommendations were NOT formally accepted by government cabinet.
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** Tendulkar used the **Urban Consumption Basket** as the universal anchor for both rural and urban poverty lines.

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which recall period methodology adopted by the C. Rangarajan Committee uses a 7-day recall period for volatile food items alongside 30-day and 365-day recall periods?  
(A) Uniform Recall Period (URP)  
(B) Mixed Recall Period (MRP)  
(C) Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP)  
(D) Annual Expenditure Period (AEP)  
**Answer: — MMRP uses 7-day recall for volatile food items (vegetables, spices, meat).

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** A commentator states that Rangarajan's poverty estimates showed lower poverty than Tendulkar's for 2011-12. Evaluate this statement against official statistics.  
**Resolution:** The statement is **FALSE**. Rangarajan set higher monetary lines (₹32/₹47 vs ₹27/₹33), resulting in a **HIGHER** poverty headcount (29.5% vs 21.9%).

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Critically compare the methodology and poverty headcount outcomes of the Tendulkar and Rangarajan Committees. How does NITI Aayog's National MPI address non-monetary deprivations?'*
🎯 Exam Angle → 🔥 HIGH — Master the distinctions between monetary policy tools (Repo vs Reverse Repo, MSF, SDF) and fiscal deficit calculation formulas.
